name: Boris Zingarevich
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: In the early 1990s Boris Zingarevich and his business partner Zakhar Smuskhin got involved in barter trading with Russian pulp and paper mills.
Later that decade, during the country's privatization phase, they bought their first plant, the Kotlas pulp and paper mill.
The partners' Ilim Group formed a joint venture in 2007 with multinational firm International Paper; the venture operates in Russia as Ilim Group.
As part of the deal, International Paper purchased 50% of Ilim for approximately $650 million, most of which was cash.
In 2023 International Paper sold its 50% interest in Ilim Group to the Russian partners.
Zingarevich also controls Ilim Timber, a large Russian processed timber firm.

name: Ruan Shuilong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Ruan Shuilong is the largest shareholder in Zhejiang Longsheng Group, a supplier of specialty chemicals and a variety of dyes.
Longsheng's predecessor organization was an insecticide factory founded in a commune set up in the eastern city of Shangyu in 1970.
Longsheng listed at Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2003.

name: Wei Huang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2024); Hurun China (2005-2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Huang Wei controls Xinhu Zhongbao, one of China's largest real estate developers.
Xinhu Zhongbao holds a minority stake in Wind, one of China's largest providers of financial information.
Huang's Xinhu Group has a controlling stake in Xiangcai Securities, a Chinese brokerage.
Huang's son Huang Licheng is a company supervisor at Xinhua Zhongbao.

name: Tang Aoqi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2025); Hurun China (2017-2025)
forbes_bio: Tang Aoqi chairs Jiangsu Xinquan Automotive Trim, a supplier of interior and exterior trim.
Customers include BYD, Nio and Great Wall Motor.
Xinquan is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Changzhou.

name: Edward Netylko
forbes_bio: Edward Netylko founded Pulse Pharmaceutical company in 1996, which became one of Russia's top three drug distributors in 2015.
In 2023, Pulse won first place in a rating of Russian pharmaceutical distributors.
The company delivers drugs to more than 60,000 pharmacies and medical institutions in Russia and employs 3,000 people.
In the1990s Netylko worked at NPO Lavochkin, a Russian aerospace company; NPO was a key contractor of the Soviet space program, Venera, which ran from 1961 to 1984.
Netylko was born in Orsha, Belarus.

name: Michael Teel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Teel is the owner and chairman of Raley's, a Sacramento-based supermarket chain with estimated revenues of $6 billion.
He is the third-generation owner. His grandfather, Tom Raley, founded the company in 1935.
He took over from his mother, Joyce Raley Teel (d. 2022), who ran Raley's from 1991 to 2015, when she transferred ownership to Michael.
Today Raley's has 235 stores in California, Nevada, Arizona, Washington, Alaska and Oregon.
The company also operates stores in several tribal nations in the Southwest.

name: Ye Guofu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Ye Guofu is the founder and CEO of budget retail chain Miniso, known for its value-for-money goods such as $1.5 mascara and $6 headphones.
The company went public on the New York Stock Exchange in October 2020.
Once branded as Japan-inspired, Miniso apologized in 2022 for its marketing strategy amid consumer backlash at home. It has has since removed Japanese elements from its store and logo designs.
Banking on a franchise-heavy model for expansion, the company now has over 5,000 Miniso shops, including more than 2,000 overseas.
Ye holds a degree from Zhongnan University of Economics and Law.

name: Alexander Linnik
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Linnik co-founded Miratorg, the leading Russian pork and beef producer, with his brother Victor, in 1995.
Miratorg is the largest owner of agricultural lands in Russia. Company controls about 1.4 million hectares, equivalent to 3.4 million acres.
Miratorg produces more than 400 products, including pork, Black Angus and Wagyu beef, pink veal, lamb ribs, sausages, poultry, frozen vegetables, dumplings and ready to eat meals.
Miratorg owns supermarket chain under brand Miratorg and restaurant chain Steak & Burger.
In 1990s Alexander and Victor Linnik earned first capital by organizing leisure activities for foreign tourists in Moscow. Then brothers started to import beef and pork from South America.
forbes_facts: Alexander and Victor Linnik are the twin brothers.

name: John Colgrove
forbes_bio: John "Coz" Colgrove is cofounder and chief visionary officer of data management and storage company Pure Storage.
He helped launch the company in 2009 and took it public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2015.
Colgrove, who owns 4% of Pure Storage, pushed for an outside CEO from the very beginning, because he was adamant about staying in a technical role.

Before cofounding Pure Storage, he joined data storage company Veritas Technologies in 1989 as a founding engineer and worked there through its IPO in 1993 and Symantec's $13.5 billion acquisition of Veritas in 2005.
Colgrove joined Palo Alto-based venture capital firm Sutter Hill Ventures in 2009 as an entrepreneur-in-residence where he met his eventual Pure Storage cofounder John Hayes.

name: Pat Neal
forbes_bio: Pat Neal founded Neal Communities, a private Florida homebuilder, in 1970.
Since then, the company has built over 25,000 homes and lots in Southwest Florida.
Neal is currently developing Skysail, a planned 640-acre community amid 240 acres of lakes in Naples that will have some 1,800 homes.
He served in the Florida state legislature from 1974 to 1986 and was also on Governor Rick Scott's transition team.
forbes_facts: Neal currently serves on the Board of Trustees of Florida Tax Watch, a non-partisan government watchdog.
Neal attended the University of Pennsylvania's business school at the same time as Donald Trump in the 1960s.
